tldr: US stocks sold off hard on Nov 5 in an AI-chip rout: the semiconductor index fell roughly 11% (its worst day since March 2020 by some reports) and Nvidia about 9%, as outlets tied it to fears that Democratic midterm wins slow the data-center buildout; closing figures vary by outlet.

The data-center backlash is now policy: Axios counts restrictive measures passing 43-1 across 10 states, Democrats are calling for a national moratorium, and OpenAI says it will avoid NDAs and keep residents from paying for power (snippet-sourced).

Moonshot put Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face (reportedly 2.8T-parameter MoE, 1M context, custom licence), while Reuters reports about 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips sit in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing's import approval.

items.title: AI chip rout: Nvidia falls about 9%, semiconductor index roughly 11% lower, S&P 500 and Nasdaq sharply down
items.summary: US stocks closed sharply lower on Nov 5, reversing Wednesday's post-election rally. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index fell about 11%, its worst day since March 2020, Nvidia closed down 9.26%, and the Nasdaq Composite fell about 5.5% into correction territory. Outlets attribute it to fears that Democratic midterm wins slow the data-center buildout, plus AI debt-cost worries and a hot inflation print. South Korea's KOSPI fell 5.28% and Japan's Nikkei 1.79% in Asia.
items.why_it_matters: The first broad market verdict on the post-election data-center backlash: chip, memory and neocloud valuations are repricing on buildout risk, which feeds directly into funding and IPO windows (Anthropic, OpenAI).

items.title: Moonshot releases Kimi K3.1 Pro weights on Hugging Face: 2.8T-parameter MoE, 1M context, custom licence
items.original_title: 月之暗面开源Kimi K3.1 Pro，登顶Agent Arena开放权重模型榜
items.summary: Moonshot AI published the weights of Kimi K3.1 Pro to Hugging Face (moonshotai/Kimi-K3.1-Pro) on Nov 4, meeting the Nov 4 deadline it set when the model launched in its API on Oct 23. Secondary reports describe a 2.8T-parameter Mixture-of-Experts with about 104B active parameters per token, a roughly 1M-token context window, text and image input, and 96 safetensors shards totalling about 1.56 TB, in an ungated repo under a custom 'Kimi K3.1 Pro License'. Chinese outlets (IT之家, 凤凰网 and others) headlined it as topping the Agent Arena open-weight ranking.
items.why_it_matters: It is the largest open-weight model released so far and, per Artificial Analysis's pre-release note, becomes the top-scoring open-weight model on its index once weights are public. At about 1.56 TB it is practical mainly for well-funded self-hosters, so the immediate effect is on hosting providers and on pricing pressure against closed frontier APIs.
key_numbers: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 55 (4th overall, pre-release)

items.title: About 600,000 Nvidia H200 chips sit in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing's import approval, Reuters reports
items.summary: Reuters, citing people familiar, reports about 600,000 H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong for possible shipment to mainland China, and Beijing has not approved large-scale imports; some outlets say customs clearance has been halted. items.title: METR analysis: Anthropic's rate of improvement on well-specified tasks has roughly doubled in a year
items.summary: The Washington Post reports an independent monitoring group (METR) estimates Anthropic's rate of AI improvement on well-specified tasks has roughly doubled over the past year. The analysis rules out increased training compute as the cause and sees AI-assisted development as a likely contributor. It is based on about 11 weeks of internal company data and employee interviews, and the authors say the estimates remain uncertain.

learn.title: Drawdown arithmetic: why an 11% drop needs a 12.4% gain to undo
learn.why_today: The item reports the semiconductor index falling about 11% in one session, with closing figures varying by outlet.
learn.explanation: Percentage returns compound multiplicatively, so a loss of d needs a gain of 1/(1+d)-1 to return to the starting level, which is always larger than |d|. Log returns, ln(1+r), add across days, which makes them convenient for aggregating and for statistics, but they differ noticeably from simple returns for large moves like this one. Quoted figures also depend on whether an outlet uses a close, an intraday low or a snapshot, so compare like with like before drawing conclusions. The numbers below are illustrative, not market data.
learn.python:
import math
# Illustrative drawdown arithmetic (the -11% is the figure in the item; the rest is toy).
drop = -0.11
need = 1 / (1 + drop) - 1          # gain needed to get back to the old level
logret = math.log(1 + drop)        # log return, additive across days
print(f"simple {drop:.1%} -> recovery needs {need:.1%}; log return {logret:.4f}")
# toy: a -11% day followed by +4%, +3% days
level = 1.0
for r in (-0.11, 0.04, 0.03):
    level *= 1 + r
print(f"after -11%, +4%, +3%: level {level:.3f} ({level-1:+.1%})")
